The main takeaway from our work is that

, although there are many factors that impact community attitudes, the most important factors are those that are within the control of the conservation manager, such as the provision of benefits and education.

, in southern Africa, communities living in and adjacent to protected areas have an understanding of the importance of conserving natural resources and, in general, have an understanding of and appreciation for the role that tourism and ecotourists play in conservation.

, in order to garner long term community support, protected areas and ecocentre managers need to be cognisant of the importance of socio-economic factors and the impact that human wildlife conflict has on attitudes and behaviour.
